- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid underreaction.  
- If recent history shows sharp spikes followed by rapid drops, model should not over-forecast the drop; apply a lagged mean reversion correction.  
- In periods with high volatility or sentiment extremes, reduce forecast granularity — avoid linear extrapolation beyond 3–5 days.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by >5% over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction proportional to sentiment magnitude.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome by >5% over 3–5 days, apply upward bias correction proportional to sentiment magnitude.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, apply a smoothing filter to avoid overfitting to recent noise.
